questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, make sure your trailer brakes are:
questions.explanation: Always lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under the trailer during coupling. This is an important safety step.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in its "normal" position when you are:
questions.explanation: The air supply control lever should be in its "normal" position when you are pulling a trailer. This keeps the system ready to work properly.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve is:

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that allows the battery to recharge efficiently.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects your tractor's brake system. It keeps air in the tractor brakes if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: Which of the following will not help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent rollover, keep cargo low and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the road shoulder will not help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Place the trailer air supply control in its "emergency" position to test:
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, test the trailer emergency brakes. Pull out the air supply control or place it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Loaded rigs are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs. The weight of the cargo raises the center of gravity.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
Any glad hand can be connected to any other glad hand.
It is best to leave one glad hand unattached.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect only matching glad hands. They are color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: When backing up while coupling a trailer, the tractor should be positioned:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and break the landing gear.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is the most likely to turn over.
questions.explanation: Make gentle, smooth turns when pulling trailers. A quick turn can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When driving a tractor-trailer equipped with ABS, you should:

options.text: Stop harder than you would otherwise.
Use extra braking force to ensure the ABS kicks in.
Brake using less pressure than you would otherwise use.

questions.explanation: Brake normally in a vehicle with ABS. Use the same braking method you would use in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost, the emergency brakes will turn on.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Use it only for parking downhill.
Use it only when carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all the air to leak out and the brakes to release. Always use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: What is the trailer hand valve used for?

options.text: To check the trailer and tractor connection.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is used to test the trailer brakes. It should be used for testing only.

questions.question: What position should the landing gear be in while driving?
questions.explanation: Always raise the landing gear completely before driving. Landing gear that is not fully raised can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: What does pushing in the trailer air supply control do?
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and turn on the emergency brakes.

questions.question: After finishing a pre-trip inspection, what should you check?

options.text: The service line valve is closed.
The trailer hand brake is on.
The emergency line valve is open.

questions.correctAnswerText: The service line valve is closed.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brakes. Listen for escaping air. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.

questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors to see if your trailer starts to skid. This lets you notice a skid as early as possible.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line. It sends air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: How can you check that air flows to all trailers before a trip?

options.text: Check for moving air inside each trailer.
Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feel for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Wait for air pressure to build. Send air to both the emergency and service lines and open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If you hear air escaping, the air is reaching all trailers.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Always make sure there is a large enough gap in traffic before entering or crossing.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the driver in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo weight low to the ground. Take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What color are emergency air lines usually coded?
questions.explanation: Service air lines are coded blue. Emergency air lines are coded red.

questions.question: How much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Before each trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: It supplies the trailer with air.
It prevents the vehicle from skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It supplies the trailer with air.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the control to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles, besides being longer?

options.text: They need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Manage space carefully when operating a combination vehicle.
